reason: The picture shows glucose entering liver cells and being joined into a stored carbohydrate, matching the first goal.
expectation: The liver cells will turn some glucose into a stored carbohydrate.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the digestive tract to the body also addresses a goal, but I chose to make the glucose store first.

effect: The liver cells stored linked glucose, completing the storage goal; I can now connect the digestive organs to the body.
reaction: It was useful to see that the store can be broken down again between meals.
reason: The remaining goal is to connect the digestive organs to the body, and the digestive tract and body model are the visible pieces for that.
expectation: The digestive tract will connect to the body and its circulation.

effect: The digestive tract is connected to circulation, completing the chapter; the colon's inner wall is still shown as unfinished.
reaction: Connecting the intestine-to-liver vein to the larger body model made the route feel more complete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Storing glucose in liver cells was most worthwhile: it connected food arriving after a meal with fuel that can be made available later.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the digestive tract was straightforward and less revealing than the storage step, though it showed the vein joining circulation.

surprise.text: The liver store was made of linked glucose units inside intact cells, and it could be broken down again when tissues need fuel.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary: the pictures and goals made both pairings clear.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, partly to see how the unfinished colon wall is assembled and what it does.
